A flaw was found in the keycloak-services component of Keycloak, which provides the core authentication and authorization logic for the identity provider. The issue occurs when a user initiates a login after visiting the password reset page, causing the system to skip mandatory security checks for Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE). This could allow an attacker who intercepts a login code to gain unauthorized access to the user's account without needing the required security verifier.

The Zion Builder  WordPress plugin through 3.6.17 does not sanitize uploaded SVG files or validate their contents before storing them in a publicly accessible location and serving them from the site's own origin, allowing authenticated users with the Author role or above to upload a crafted SVG containing JavaScript that executes in the browser of anyone who opens the file.

Improper neutralization of input during web page generation ('cross-site scripting') in Microsoft Authentication Library for JavaScript allows an unauthorized attacker to perform spoofing over a network.

The Elementor Website Builder  WordPress plugin before 4.3.6 does not validate or escape an element identifier before rendering it into a client-side framework attribute that is evaluated as JavaScript, allowing users with the Contributor role to store scripts that execute in the browser of anyone viewing the affected content, including an administrator reviewing the submission for publication.

A certificate validation bypass in Node.js https.Agent lets a cached TLS session authenticated under one CA policy be reused by a later request with a stricter policy. https.Agent.prototype.getName() assigns the same Agent and session-cache key to a request that omits ca and one that explicitly supplies ca: [], because an omitted value appends nothing to the key while an empty array stringifies to an empty string. The two policies differ: omitting ca uses the default trust store, while supplying ca replaces it. Since they share a key, a TLS session authenticated under the broader default policy is handed to a new connection made under the later ca: [] policy, and TLS 1.3 session resumption carries the earlier authentication forward, so the second request reports authorized === true and transmits confidential data to a server its own CA policy would reject on a fresh connection. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

pgEdge Postgres MCP Server enables SQL queries against PostgreSQL databases through Model Context Protocol compatible clients. Prior to 1.1.0, the bundled CLI and web clients classified query_database statements only by their first keyword before deciding whether to display a write confirmation. SELECT INTO, data-modifying common table expressions beginning with WITH, and EXPLAIN ANALYZE of a write were treated as reads and could execute without confirmation on an allow_writes connection. Read-only connections remain protected by PostgreSQL transaction access mode, and EXPLAIN without ANALYZE and SELECT FOR UPDATE remain classified as reads. This issue is fixed in 1.1.0.

The Flatsome WordPress theme before 3.20.13 does not sanitise post meta saved through an AJAX action, nor escape it when rendering the product page, allowing users with a role as low as Contributor (who lack the unfiltered_html capability) to store JavaScript that executes in the browser of anyone who views the product, including administrators.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. When a client application enforces step-up authentication or multi-factor authentication (MFA) via a minimum authentication level, Keycloak fails to apply this requirement to login sessions initiated through the credential reset endpoint. An attacker who possesses a user's initial credentials (such as a password) can navigate from the reset interface back to the standard login form and authenticate without completing the required second factor. This flaw allows an attacker to obtain valid access tokens and gain unauthorized access to protected services without satisfying mandatory security controls.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. When evaluating access permissions, Keycloak Authorization Services improperly matches resource paths containing wildcard file extensions by evaluating only the file extension suffix and ignoring configured path prefixes. An authenticated remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by requesting a restricted resource that shares a file extension with a more permissive resource, leading to an authorization bypass and unintended access to protected data.

A flaw was found in the group-move and organization group reparenting endpoints of the keycloak-services component. This component is responsible for core authentication and authorization services in the Red Hat build of Keycloak. The issue occurs because the system fails to check if a target parent group confers administrative roles when a group is moved. A delegated administrator can exploit this to move a group they control under an administrative group, causing all members to inherit full realm-admin privileges and gain complete control over the realm.

Mongoose is a MongoDB object modeling tool designed to work in an asynchronous environment. Prior to 6.13.12, 7.8.13, 8.24.7, and 9.11.4, Schema.prototype.virtual() builds nested virtual paths without applying the special-property validation already used by Schema.path() and Schema.add(). An attacker who can influence virtual field names in dynamic schemas, content-management form builders, or schema-as-code systems can supply path segments such as __proto__, constructor, or prototype, causing the virtual-path reducer to write enumerable properties to Object.prototype or Function.prototype. The resulting prototype pollution can spoof inherited property checks such as authorization flags and can provide function-prototype gadget state to other server-side JavaScript code. This issue is fixed in versions 6.13.12, 7.8.13, 8.24.7, and 9.11.4.

SAP NetWeaver Application Server Java (NWDI Cockpit)� does not perform sufficient authorization checks for certain functionality that retrieves sensitive information. An attacker with low privileges could send a specially crafted request to access sensitive information belonging to other system users. Successful exploitation results in a high impact on confidentiality, with no impact on integrity or availability of the application.

SAP NetWeaver Application Server Java (NWDI Cockpit) does not perform sufficient authorization checks for certain functionality before processing the requests. An attacker with low privileges could exploit this to perform unauthorized modifications. Successful exploitation results in high impact on integrity, with no impact on confidentiality and availability of the application.

pgEdge Postgres MCP Server enables SQL queries against PostgreSQL databases through Model Context Protocol compatible clients. Prior to 1.1.0, deployments exposing the nondefault HTTP transport with authentication enabled used the leftmost caller-supplied X-Forwarded-For value as the client address for login rate limiting. ExtractIPAddress in internal/auth/middleware.go supplied that value to IsAllowed and RecordFailedAttempt in internal/auth/rate_limiter.go, allowing an unauthenticated caller to rotate addresses to evade throttling or assert another user's address to consume that user's limiter bucket. The published nginx configuration appended rather than replaced X-Forwarded-For, making the issue reachable without an operator misconfiguration. Username-keyed account lockout did not use the client address, but shipped defaults disabled that separate control through MaxFailedAttemptsBeforeLockout: 0. This issue is fixed in version 1.1.0.

pgEdge Postgres MCP Server enables SQL queries against PostgreSQL databases through Model Context Protocol compatible clients. Prior to 1.1.0, the where parameter of the count_rows tool accepted subqueries against tables other than the table named in the tool call. A caller could use predicates and the returned row count as an inference oracle to extract data from any other table that the connected database role could read. The database privilege boundary remained intact, and the flaw did not grant access to tables outside that role's existing SELECT privileges. This issue is fixed in version 1.1.0.
Insufficiently protected credentials in Microsoft Authentication Library (MSAL) for Node.js allows an unauthorized attacker to disclose information over a network.

A cleartext storage flaw was found in the AAP Gateway Operator. When reconciling an AutomationController, the operator reads the protected resource-server Secret (Secret/<aap-name>-resource-server, key controller_resource_server_secret) and copies its plaintext value into the generated AutomationController custom resource under spec.extra_settings (RESOURCE_SERVER.SECRET_KEY). Although the operator uses no_log to keep the value out of its own logs, serializing it into the custom resource exposes it to any principal able to read the AutomationController CR without permission to read the backing Kubernetes Secret, breaking the expected OpenShift RBAC separation between the two resources. The value may also propagate into Kubernetes API/etcd storage, GitOps and Argo diffs and history, rendered manifests, support bundles, and audit data. The resource-server secret is intended for trusted Gateway-to-Controller service authentication, and its disclosure may allow a user to impersonate a trusted Controller service and reach privileged service-index APIs.

Buffer over-read in PostgreSQL parallel B-tree scans allows an object creator to read attacker-chosen server-memory addresses, via a function incorrectly marked PARALLEL SAFE or STABLE to make participating workers build different scan-key arrays.  Within major versions 17-18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7 and 17.12 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 17 are unaffected.

The MongoDB Node.js driver does not consistently enforce its permitted-host restriction during OIDC authentication. A bearer token produced by the embedding application's own login callback may therefore be transmitted to a host outside the configured set of permitted hosts, which may result in unintended disclosure of that credential. No database account is required; the party supplying the connection configuration needs only to influence the settings the application passes to the driver.

Dockhand before 1.0.55 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that lets users holding only containers:view download arbitrary container files instead of requiring containers:exec. Authenticated Enterprise RBAC users can request any path from the files/download endpoint, which reads through Docker's archive API, to retrieve secrets, keys, and mounted credentials.

Keep 0.34.10 through 0.55.0 contains a blind SQL injection vulnerability in its CEL-to-SQL converter, which inserts bracket-indexed JSON keys from CEL filters unescaped into JSON path expressions for SQLite, PostgreSQL, and MySQL. Authenticated users with read:alert permission can submit crafted CEL expressions to /alerts/query or the cel parameter of /incidents, using result counts as a boolean oracle to extract other tenants' alerts and password hashes.

Vulnerability in the Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition product of Oracle Java SE (component: Hotspot).  Supported versions that are affected are Oracle Java SE: 8u511b33-perf, 11.0.33.0.3, 17.0.21.0.3, 21.0.13.0.3, 25.0.5.0.3, 27.0.1.0.3; Oracle GraalVM for JDK: 17.0.21.0.3 and  21.0.13.0.3; Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition: 21.3.20.0.3. Difficult to exploit vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized ability to cause a hang or frequently repeatable crash (complete DOS) of Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition as well as  unauthorized update, insert or delete access to some of Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition accessible data. Note: This vulnerability can be exploited by using APIs in the specified Component, e.g., through a web service which supplies data to the APIs. This vulnerability also applies to Java deployments, typically in clients running sandboxed Java Web Start applications or sandboxed Java applets, that load and run untrusted code (e.g., code that comes from the internet) and rely on the Java sandbox for security. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 6.5 (Integrity and Availability impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:H).

Vulnerability in the Oracle Platform Security for Java product of Oracle Fusion Middleware (component: Centralized Thirdparty Jars).  Supported versions that are affected are 12.2.1.4.0 and  14.1.2.0.0. Difficult to exploit vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via HTTP to compromise Oracle Platform Security for Java.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle Platform Security for Java accessible data as well as  unauthorized update, insert or delete access to some of Oracle Platform Security for Java accessible data. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 6.5 (Confidentiality and Integrity impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:L/A:N).

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a credential exposure vulnerability in the connection-test endpoint that allows authorized integration users to redirect stored credentials by overriding connection host, port, and user fields. Attackers can point the test at a server they control to capture offline-crackable PostgreSQL md5 or MySQL handshakes and recover the stored database password.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator or Owner users to execute database functions by supplying zero-argument function calls as column default values. Attackers can plant functions like version() or inet_server_addr() in PostgreSQL or MySQL column definitions and read results through record APIs, disclosing server addresses, role names, and engine details.

WatchAlert 2.0.0 through 3.9.20 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in the /api/w8t/datasource/dataSourceGet endpoint that lets authenticated users read other tenants' datasources because lookups omit tenant_id filtering. Tenant members with datasource view permission can request another tenant's datasource ID to obtain basic auth passwords, AWS and Alibaba Cloud keys, and Kubernetes kubeconfigs.

@fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server. In versions before 11.6.10, it rejects destinations containing parent-directory path segments by an exact string match, so a segment that carries a semicolon path parameter, such as a dot-dot segment followed by a semicolon and an optional parameter, is not equal to the plain dot-dot form and passes the check, and the WHATWG URL parser keeps it as an ordinary segment so the rewrite-prefix containment check also passes. Servlet containers such as Apache Tomcat and Jetty strip semicolon path parameters from each segment before resolving dot-segments, so a request routed through the configured prefix is rewritten and reaches the upstream where it resolves above the intended subtree, escaping the path the proxy is meant to expose and, on some containers, crossing application contexts. Both the HTTP and WebSocket proxy paths are affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.10, and users should upgrade to 11.6.10 or later.

LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.9, GET /api/permissions/search-principals passes the q parameter to JavaScript RegExp construction and MongoDB regex queries in packages/data-schemas/src/methods/userGroup.ts findGroupsByNamePattern and searchPrincipals without escaping metacharacters. An authenticated user with people-picker permission can submit a catastrophic-backtracking pattern that blocks the Node.js event loop and makes the service unresponsive to concurrent users; invalid patterns can also produce server errors. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.9.

ArcadeDB before 26.11.1 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read schema definitions of denied types through listings ignoring per-type ACLs. Attackers can query the PostgreSQL wire catalog, GraphQL introspection, or MCP get_schema to reveal property names, indexes, inheritance, and materialized view SQL.

Heym before 0.0.148 passes Playwright navigate-step URLs to page.goto() without validating the scheme and runs step-based scripts inside the backend container. A signed-in user who can run workflows can navigate to file:// URLs and use getText to read known-path files such as the Kubernetes ServiceAccount token or Docker secrets.

HedgeDoc before 1.12.1 contains a prototype pollution vulnerability in the POST /history/:noteId endpoint that allows authenticated users to modify Object.prototype by supplying __proto__ as the noteId. Attackers can send a pinned value to /history/__proto__, which historyPost() in lib/history.js assigns onto the prototype, crashing the Node.js process and causing denial of service for all users.

Laradocs maintains version-controlled documentation inside a Laravel codebase. From version 0.4.0 to before version 1.0.0, Laradocs is vulnerable to local command injection in server-side KaTeX rendering via an unescaped Node.js binary path in a proc_open() command string. This issue has been patched in version 1.0.0.

The Flatsome theme for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'data-text-sec', 'data-title', and 'title' Attributes via Custom HTML Block in all versions up to, and including, 3.20.12 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The payload survives server-side sanitization because wp_kses_post permits data-* attributes globally via _wp_add_global_attributes, allowing attacker-controlled values in data-text-sec, data-title, and title attributes to persist in saved post content and be later interpreted as HTML by the ux-countdown, scroll-to, and lightbox-gallery JavaScript behaviors.

Silverstripe Framework is a PHP framework which powers the Silverstripe CMS. Prior to 6.2.13, the HTML sanitiser does not normalize certain control bytes that browsers ignore when parsing URLs. A CMS author can place those bytes before a javascript: URL in stored content so the sanitiser misses the dangerous scheme, and JavaScript executes in the browser of another user who views the content. This issue is fixed in version 6.2.13.

Obot from 0.9.0 before 0.27.0 contains a command injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users to execute shell commands by embedding an EOF line in file-type MCP server configuration values. Attackers can terminate the heredoc in the generated init container script to run commands, modify the MCP server files volume, and reach services on Obot's Docker network.

A vulnerability was detected in erupts erupt up to 2.3.0. Affected by this issue is the function ReportService.queryBiData of the file ReportService.java. Performing a manipulation of the argument sort results in sql injection. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. Upgrading to version 2.4.0 can resolve this issue. The patch is named 8d2eaffc79b977c9d11222b9d435a002dceaa062. It is suggested to upgrade the affected component.

Tencent BrowserSkill through 0.4.2 contains a missing authentication vulnerability that allows local attackers to impersonate the bsk daemon because remoteSocket() connects to the loopback WebSocket without credentials or peer verification. Attackers who bind the daemon port before it starts or after it exits receive the extension's full tool surface, including evaluate, to run JavaScript through CDP in logged-in browser tabs.

A vulnerability was found in tjake Jlama up to 0.8.4/0.9.0-beta. Affected by this vulnerability is the function SafeTensorIndex.loadWeights of the file jlama-core/src/main/java/com/github/tjake/jlama/safetensors/SafeTensorIndex.java. Performing a manipulation of the argument weight_map results in path traversal. The attack may be initiated remotely. The exploit has been made public and could be used. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in interface/billing/sl_eob_invoice.php, which escapes billing codes for HTML attributes but not for JavaScript strings in an inline onkeyup handler. Clinicians with encounter coding access can save crafted billing codes through diagnosis.php that execute script when a Back Office user enters a payment, exposing patient and financial data or performing actions as that user.

Connaisseur is an admission controller that integrates container image signature verification into a Kubernetes cluster. Prior to 3.11.1, the Cosign validator counts valid signature layers rather than distinct trust roots for trustRoot: "*" policies using an explicit threshold or an implicit require-all policy. An attacker who controls one configured trust root's signing key and can attach multiple signatures to an image can satisfy a threshold intended to require multiple independent roots, causing admission without the intended signer quorum. Policies using a single trust root or the required option are not affected. This issue is fixed in 3.11.1.

A vulnerability has been found in xuxueli xxl-job 3.5.0/3.5.1-SNAPSHOT. Affected is the function difyWorkflowJobHandler of the file xxl-job-executor-sample-springboot-ai/src/main/java/com/xxl/job/executor/jobhandler/AIXxlJob.java of the component AI Executor. The manipulation of the argument baseUrl leads to server-side request forgery. The attack may be initiated remotely. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

Node.js discloses proxy credentials in ERR_PROXY_INVALID_CONFIG error messages. CVE-2026-48615 established that a proxy credential must not appear in a Node.js error message and redacted the username and password from ProxyConfig.href, but that fix missed four error paths in the same subsystem, one of them inside the same constructor, which interpolate the raw proxy URL, credentials included, into an ERR_PROXY_INVALID_CONFIG message. The proxy URL comes from the environment, but the defect is the sink: a secret that Node.js redacts everywhere else is emitted verbatim into a much wider audience than the process environment, such as stderr, container logs, log aggregation, and crash reporting services. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

SAP NetWeaver Application Server Java (Web Dynpro Java) does not sufficiently validate certain request parameters used to resolve styling resources in the application. An unauthenticated attacker could craft a malicious link that, when clicked by an authenticated victim, causes the victim's browser to load attacker-controlled styling content within the trusted application context. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to redress the trusted user interface for phishing purposes and exfiltrate limited web page content, resulting in a low impact on confidentiality and integrity. There is no impact on availability.

A reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in the conversion-statistics pages of Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute JavaScript in an authenticated user's browser by persuading them to visit a crafted URL. An incorrect ownership check validates the advertiser identifier instead of the supplied website identifier, allowing malicious website input to reach HTML output without appropriate encoding. A related output issue affects the hour parameter. The issue is fixed in Revive Adserver 6.0.9 by validating the correct website identifier and normalising the hour parameter before formatting.

A reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in the iframe invocation options of Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute JavaScript in an authenticated user's browser by persuading them to visit a crafted URL. When generating invocation tags for an any-size zone, the frame_width and frame_height request parameters are included in HTML attributes without appropriate encoding. The issue is fixed in Revive Adserver 6.0.9 by HTML-encoding the affected values in the invocation-option form fields.

A reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in updates-history.php in Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute JavaScript in a victim's browser by persuading them to visit a crafted URL. Attacker-controlled values are included in XML command attributes without appropriate encoding, allowing injection of executable XHTML into the response. The preliminary session check omits GET xajax requests, exposing an unauthenticated attack path, while authenticated administrator requests also reach the unsafe output. The issue is fixed in Revive Adserver 6.0.9 by applying the session check to both GET and POST requests and encoding XML command attribute values in both response serializers.

A stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the report date-selection controls of Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute JavaScript in a victim's browser by persuading them to follow a crafted report URL and complete normal reauthentication. An attacker-controlled period_preset value can be saved in the victim's session and inserted into JavaScript without appropriate encoding. The payload can execute on the initial report view and subsequent report views using the stored defaults. The issue is fixed in Revive Adserver 6.0.9 by applying JSON encoding appropriate for the JavaScript context to date-selection values.

A reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability exists in the web user interface of multiple versions of OpenNMS Meridian and Horizon. Several web UI pages copy request parameter values into the HTML response without correct contextual output encoding. A remote attacker can craft a link that runs arbitrary JavaScript in the OpenNMS origin when an authenticated user opens it. The script runs in the victim's browser with the victim's session, so the attacker can read page data and send same-origin requests as the victim. The fix encodes the affected request values. On pages that use AngularJS, the fix also stops client-side template evaluation of the reflected values.



The solution is to upgrade to Meridian 2024.3.15, 2025.0.12, 2026.0.2 and Horizon 36.0.6 or newer. Meridian and Horizon installation instructions state that they are intended for installation within an organization's private networks and should not be directly accessible from the Internet.

Zipline before 3.7.12 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability in the login page that allows attackers to execute JavaScript by supplying an unvalidated url parameter. Attackers can craft a login link with a javascript: URI in the url parameter that executes in the victim's browser after login.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in the ACL module that allows attackers to execute JavaScript in authenticated sessions via the module_id parameter. Attackers can deliver crafted acl/index or acl/acl links that inject unencoded input into inline script blocks, stealing non-HttpOnly session cookies and modifying ACL configuration.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers to execute JavaScript by injecting payloads into the searchEleNo POST parameter of the application/index/search endpoint. Attackers can break out of unencoded HTML attributes in auto-suggest.phtml to inject event handlers that fire on DOM insertion, stealing non-HttpOnly session cookies and patient data.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in the Application module's auto-suggest endpoint, which echoes the searchMode POST parameter unencoded into a single-quoted onClick attribute. Attackers can induce an authenticated user to submit a single-quote payload to application/index/search, executing arbitrary JavaScript in that user's session to steal session cookies or disclose patient data.

BuildAdmin 1.0.1 through 2.3.9 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to store javascript: URLs in the admin operation log via the X-Rewrite-URL header. When an administrator clicks the log entry's url open button, the script runs in the backend origin and steals the adminInfo token from localStorage, enabling account takeover.

IBM Cyber Fraud 1.0.0 through 1.1.0 is vulnerable to cross-site scripting. This vulnerability allows an unauthenticated attacker to embed arbitrary JavaScript code in the Web UI thus altering the intended functionality potentially leading to credentials disclosure within a trusted session.

Kroki before 0.36.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in the /dbml/svg endpoint that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject javascript: hyperlinks by supplying crafted DBML table url, headercolor, or TableGroup color settings. Attackers can send a crafted SVG link that, when opened and the table header clicked, executes attacker JavaScript in the Kroki origin.

Kroki before 0.36.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts via unvalidated svg-color-dark-scheme and svg-color-light-scheme options. Attackers can craft a GET /goat/svg URL whose option value closes the SVG style element, executing JavaScript in the Kroki origin when victims open it.

AdminNeo before 5.9.1 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in EditorNeo that allows remote attackers to execute JavaScript by injecting quote characters into the request URI. Attackers can lure authenticated users to crafted edit links whose path breaks out of the CSP-nonced whisper script in editor/core/Admin.php, enabling session theft and database credential disclosure.

PMB 7.3.1 before 7.3.15 and 7.4.x before 7.4.5 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject script through unescaped POST parameter names. Attackers can send crafted parameter names to opac_css/index.php extended_search, which empr.inc.php and languages.inc.php reflect into hidden form inputs to execute JavaScript. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-23.

Reddit Top RSS through commit 5e38bfd contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through the unescaped score GET parameter. Attackers can craft links with a score value that closes the input value attribute in html.php, executing JavaScript in victims' browsers. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-19.

JoomBri Careers 3.3.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through the 'keyword' parameter of the /for-jobseekers/search-jobs endpoint in com_jbcareers. Attackers can craft malicious URLs using an attribute-breakout payload with onfocus and autofocus to execute arbitrary JavaScript and steal session tokens or credentials. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-23.

Tiki Wiki CMS Groupware 12.12 through 12.14, 15.5 before 18.10, 19.0 before 21.9, 22.0 before 24.3, and 25.0 contain a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through the objectId parameter of tiki-ajax_services.php. Attackers can send a crafted GET request with the comment controller and list action to execute arbitrary JavaScript and steal session tokens or credentials. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-19.

phpLDAPadmin 1.1.0 before 1.2.5 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through the dn parameter of cmd.php?cmd=template_engine. Attackers can supply an unparseable dn value that pretty_print_dn returns unescaped in the 'No such entry' error, executing JavaScript in victims' browsers. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-23.

Bagisto 2.1.0 before 2.2.1 contains a client-side template injection vulnerability in the search page where the 'query' parameter is rendered unescaped inside a Vue app root. Unauthenticated attackers can send crafted VueJS template expressions to the /bagisto-common/search endpoint via the 'query' parameter to execute arbitrary JavaScript in victims' browsers. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2024-07-30.

Retool versions 3.253.0 before 3.253.19, 3.254.0 before 3.284.12, and 3.285.0 before 3.300.4 contain a DOM-based cross-site scripting vulnerability in the custom-component-collections.html postMessage handler that imports received code without origin validation. Unauthenticated attackers can send crafted postMessage events that load attacker-controlled code via data:text/javascript URIs to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's context. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2026-04-22.

cPanel & WHM 11.134.0.13 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through the mpidentity parameter of /mailman/listinfo. Attackers can send crafted requests with a script-context breakout payload in mpidentity to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2026-06-08.

A stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the Public News Article Rendering Module of PHPGurukul News Portal Project v4.1 allows authenticated attackers with administrative or sub-administrative privileges to inject arbitrary HTML and JavaScript through the postdescription parameter when creating or editing news articles. The application renders the stored post content without proper output encoding in news-details.php, allowing injected JavaScript to execute in the browsers of users who visit the affected article.

A Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability exists in PHPGurukul News Portal Project V4.1. The $currenturl variable in news-details.php is constructed using unencoded REQUEST_URI and HTTP_HOST server variables and echoed directly into the href attributes of social share links. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this by crafting a URL containing HTML metacharacters to break out of the href attribute and execute arbitrary HTML or JavaScript in the context of the victim's browser.

SemanticMediaWiki from 3.0.0 before 7.4.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in CsvFileExportPrinter and DsvResultPrinter via unescaped valuesep and separator parameters. Attackers can craft Special:Ask links using request_type=special_page so export output renders as text/html, executing JavaScript in victims' browsers under the wiki origin.

IBM Engineering AI Hub 1.0.0 through 1.4.0 is vulnerable to cross-site scripting. This vulnerability allows an unauthenticated attacker to embed arbitrary JavaScript code in the Web UI thus altering the intended functionality potentially leading to credentials disclosure within a trusted session.
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2 reflected XSS in Kubernetes cloud profile namespace and deployment choosers was possible

MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. From 6.0 until 8.6.5, MapServer's WMS OpenLayers output, selected by FORMAT=application/openlayers or template=openlayers, substitutes a request-derived online-resource value into a single-quoted JavaScript string in src/maptemplate.c. The prior remediation for GHSA-xqj6-vjqr-33vv used msEscapeJSonLikeString() to protect the JavaScript string but did not neutralize angle brackets, so attacker-controlled X-Forwarded-Host or X-Forwarded-Proto values can still terminate the script element at the HTML parser layer. Deployments that expose attacker-controlled PATH_INFO or map= values reaching the same string are also affected. An unauthenticated attacker can cause arbitrary JavaScript to execute in a victim's browser under the MapServer origin when the victim loads the crafted output. This issue is fixed in version 8.6.5.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. From 4.5.00 until 4.5.13 and 4.6.02, an unauthenticated attacker can place a multiply encoded value in the news module search q parameter. $nv_Request->get_title() decodes and sanitizes the input once, but modules/news/funcs/search.php subsequently applies urldecode() after sanitization. The resulting raw keyword reaches the {KEY} search-input attribute through search_theme() and the no-results element through search_result_theme() in the default and mobile themes, permitting attribute or tag injection and same-origin JavaScript execution when a victim opens the crafted search URL. This issue is fixed in versions 4.5.13 and 4.6.02.

pgEdge RAG Server is an API server for retrieval-augmented generation over PostgreSQL content using pgvector. Prior to 2.0.0, the BM25 keyword index is a single per-pipeline object shared by the unauthenticated query endpoint, and concurrent requests lock its clear, refill, and search operations separately. This allows one request to search a corpus populated through another request's search filter, which can return documents belonging to a different tenant or customer without malformed input. The affected responses cannot be identified retrospectively from the server logs. This issue is fixed in version 2.0.0.

Forge (also called node-forge) is a native implementation of Transport Layer Security in JavaScript. Prior to 1.4.3, a forge.tls client accepts a ServerHello compression_method that it did not offer. When the client later handles ServerHelloDone, tls.createConnectionState() rejects the unsupported compression algorithm by throwing an Error that propagates from connection.process(). A malicious server or an on-path attacker can alter the unauthenticated ServerHello compression byte before the server Finished message and terminate a Node.js process when the application does not catch the exception. The affected client paths include direct forge.tls use, forge.tls.wrapSocket, and forge.http; forge.tls servers are not affected, and the issue has no confidentiality or integrity impact. This issue is fixed in version 1.4.3.

Forge (also called node-forge) is a native implementation of Transport Layer Security in JavaScript. From 0.1.2 until 1.4.3, forge.http uses _trimString() in lib/http.js to remove trailing whitespace from response header values and cookie names and values with a regular expression that can take quadratic time. A malicious server or on-path attacker can supply a long whitespace run followed by a non-whitespace character in a response header, causing response.readHeader() or response.getCookies() to repeatedly scan the input and block the Node.js event loop or browser tab for minutes. Applications are affected only when they use forge.http with a socket pool to communicate with an untrusted server; forge.http is not loaded by require('node-forge'), and the issue has no confidentiality or integrity impact. This issue is fixed in version 1.4.3.

Forge (also called node-forge) is a native implementation of Transport Layer Security in JavaScript. Prior to 1.4.3, a forge.tls client can pass a handshake record to tls.handleHandshake() while the connection has no session, including after a close_notify alert, after the application calls close(), or before handshake() is called. The handler dereferences c.session.md5 before dispatching the message, causing a TypeError to propagate from connection.process(). A malicious server or on-path attacker can deliver the record, including after a reset when the connection uses no encryption, and terminate a Node.js process if the application does not catch the exception. forge.tls servers are not affected, and there is no confidentiality or integrity impact. This issue is fixed in version 1.4.3.

A one-byte heap buffer overflow in Node.js HTTP/2 Alt-Svc handling lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker corrupt process memory. When an application passes an attacker-controlled value such as a request's :authority header to Http2Session.altsvc(), the AltSvc implementation in src/node_http2.cc allocates a buffer sized to the origin length and then writes it with a null terminator, placing one byte past the end of the allocation. A single request carrying a long but syntactically valid :authority triggers the out-of-bounds write, which aborts the process and serves as a remote heap-corruption primitive. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x and 24.x.

An unauthenticated HTTP/2 client can exhaust Node.js server memory because inbound DATA queued on an undrained stream is charged to no session budget. Each inbound DATA frame creates one JavaScript Buffer view in the receiving stream's readable queue, but nothing charges that queue to current_session_memory_: the socket read buffer is accounted only during parsing and released immediately, so whatever stays queued is accounted to nothing. A peer that fills a stream's receive window with one-byte DATA frames pays about 10 wire bytes per frame while the server retains about 114 bytes per frame, so a single stream on one connection can retain hundreds of megabytes from tens of megabytes sent. maxSessionMemory neither bounds the growth nor refuses new streams, because Http2Session::CanAddStream gates admission on the same counter that never sees the queue. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x and 24.x.

A NULL pointer dereference in Node.js HTTP/2 lets an unauthenticated client crash the server, over both TLS and cleartext, by cancelling file downloads. When the server serves a file with stream.respondWithFile() or stream.respondWithFD() and the client cancels the request, a StreamPipe used for the transfer is torn down in an order that leaves a NULL pointer which is then dereferenced, aborting the process. No crafted frames are needed, and a handful of cancelled requests against a default file-serving handler is enough. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

basic-ftp is an FTP client for Node.js. Prior to 6.2.3, FTPContext.send() throws when a command contains carriage return, line feed, or NUL characters, but calls made from response handlers execute synchronously inside the control socket's data event without an exception boundary. In Client.login(), an attacker-influenced password reaches the PASS command after a server sends a 331 response, and in a resumed download an attacker-influenced remote path reaches the RETR command after a 350 response to REST. The resulting exception does not reject client.access() or downloadTo(), escapes ordinary promise error handling, and terminates the Node.js process, while the validation guard still prevents command injection. This issue is fixed in version 6.2.3.

create-ecdh is a browserifiable implementation of Node.js crypto.createECDH. In versions 4.0.4 and below, the JavaScript implementation (browser.js, used by browser bundlers and on Node.js versions without a working native crypto.createECDH) did not validate peer public keys in ECDH.prototype.computeSecret or ECDH.prototype.setPublicKey. The peer point was multiplied by the local private key without checking that it was on the configured curve or in its prime-order subgroup. An attacker who can submit public keys to a party that reuses a static private key can perform an invalid-curve or small-subgroup attack and recover the private key modulo small factors, eventually recovering the full key via the Chinese Remainder Theorem. For the ed25519 and curve25519 curves, low-order points were also accepted, which could force a predictable shared secret. On modern Node.js, create-ecdh re-exports the native implementation, which is not affected. This issue is fixed in version 4.0.5.

SQLBot 1.10.0 through 1.10.3 fails to apply its PostgreSQL dangerous-function denylist because DS_SPECIFIC_DANGEROUS_FUNCTIONS uses 'postgresql' while lookups use the 'pg' type. Authenticated users can steer LLM-generated SQL past check_sql_read() using pg_read_file, pg_write_file, lo_import or lo_export to read or write files on the database host.

Vulnerability in the Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition product of Oracle Java SE (component: Core Java Libraries).  Supported versions that are affected are Oracle Java SE: 8u511b33, 8u511b33-perf, 11.0.33.0.3, 17.0.21.0.3, 21.0.13.0.3, 25.0.5.0.3, 27.0.1.0.3; Oracle GraalVM for JDK: 17.0.21.0.3 and  21.0.13.0.3; Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition: 21.3.20.0.3. Difficult to exploit vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized creation, deletion or modification access to critical data or all Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition accessible data. Note: This vulnerability can be exploited by using APIs in the specified Component, e.g., through a web service which supplies data to the APIs. This vulnerability also applies to Java deployments, typically in clients running sandboxed Java Web Start applications or sandboxed Java applets, that load and run untrusted code (e.g., code that comes from the internet) and rely on the Java sandbox for security. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 5.9 (Integrity impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N).

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, an unauthenticated user with network-path interception capability could cause attacker-controlled JavaScript to run in the browser of a security analyst who previews a Portable Document Format (PDF) attachment in Mission Control. The JavaScript could expose data and perform actions available to the security analyst.
The vulnerability is possible because Mission Control loads the PDF rendering worker from an external content delivery network.
The vulnerability requires the unauthenticated user to intercept the network path to the external content delivery network and a security analyst to preview a PDF attachment in Mission Control. The unauthenticated user should not be able to exploit the vulnerability at will.
For more information see Collaborate on investigations in Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.7/investigations/collaborate-on-investigations-in-splunk-enterprise-security) in the Splunk documentation.

Due to a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in SAP NetWeaver AS Java (Web Services), an unauthenticated attacker could craft a SOAP request that causes the server to return a SOAP fault to a URL under the attacker�s control. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to disclose information about connected systems, impacting confidentiality, while integrity and availability remain unaffected.

pgEdge RAG Server is an API server for retrieval-augmented generation over PostgreSQL content using pgvector. Prior to 2.0.0, the unauthenticated query API in internal/server/handlers.go returns err.Error() from failed LLM provider calls, preserving provider-controlled error text that can quote a partially masked submitted API key. A remote caller can cause an authentication failure and obtain part of the operator's credential for the third-party provider account through the query API error response. This issue is fixed in version 2.0.0.

OpenTelemetry JavaScript is the OpenTelemetry JavaScript client. From 0.204.0 until 0.222.0, @opentelemetry/instrumentation-http writes the raw query string from incoming HTTP requests to the url.query server-span attribute without applying the redactedQueryParams protection used for outgoing spans. Services receiving signed URLs or other credentials in query parameters can therefore export still-valid secrets to tracing backends, where observability infrastructure and users with span-read access may read them. The redactedQueryParams option does not protect incoming spans in affected versions. This issue is fixed in version 0.222.0.

Mikochi is a minimalist file manager with streaming capabilities. Prior to 1.10.1, authenticated users of bare-metal instances configured with a non-default trailing-slash DATA_DIR can use the Move endpoint to supply traversal-containing source or destination paths. The affected path validation can resolve those paths outside the configured data directory, allowing files to be written beyond Mikochi's intended storage boundary. Docker deployments that confine the data directory to a mounted volume and configurations whose DATA_DIR lacks a trailing slash are not affected by the described attack. This issue is fixed in version 1.10.1.

An insecure default initialization of resource in the Tomcat shutdown listener of Ivanti Sentry before versions 11.0, 10.8.3, and 10.7.4 allows a local authenticated attacker to cause a denial of service.

MicroQuickJS (mquickjs) before commit 99eed3f contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability because JS_Call() raises exceptions during frame setup without updating ctx->sp and ctx->fp. Attackers can supply JavaScript that calls a non-function value, causing build_backtrace() to walk stale frame pointers and crash the engine for denial of service.

cassandra-jdbc-wrapper provides a JDBC-compliant API over the Java driver for Apache Cassandra. Prior to 4.16.4 and 5.0.2, DriverUtil.toStringWithoutSensitiveValues() and DriverUtil.redactSensitiveValuesInJdbcUrl() redact the password property but not the equally sensitive token property used for DataStax Astra and other token-based authentication. When DEBUG logging is enabled, SessionHolder passes connection properties and JDBC URLs containing token through these helpers, causing the live token to be written in plaintext when connections are acquired or released. An attacker who can read those logs can use the token to access Cassandra data and operations authorized to that credential. This issue is fixed in versions 4.16.4 and 5.0.2.

A vulnerability was found in fushengqian fuintCatering up to 6d054f5788ac8645eb491f79242bb8a625efc133. The affected element is the function updateCommissionCash of the file CommissionCashServiceImpl.java. The manipulation of the argument Status results in improper access controls. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. This product takes the approach of rolling releases to provide continious delivery. Therefore, version details for affected and updated releases are not available. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A vulnerability has been found in DataLinkDC dinky up to 1.2.5. Affected by this issue is the function CatalogueController.upload of the file dinky-admin/src/main/java/org/dinky/controller/CatalogueController.java of the component Catalogue Upload API. The manipulation leads to path traversal. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The researcher claims to have submitted a GHSA on the repository of the project.

ModSecurity is an open source, cross platform web application firewall (WAF) engine for Apache, IIS and Nginx. Prior to 2.9.15 and 3.0.17, msre_fn_removeComments_execute in apache2/re_tfns.c and inplace() in src/actions/transformations/remove_comments.cc implement t:removeComments by copying the character immediately after a comment terminator without re-evaluating it. Adjacent comments can therefore leave a later comment in the transformed value, allowing inline-comment obfuscation to bypass rules that depend on comment stripping. When a comment terminator is the final content, the same copy reads one byte beyond the input buffer. This issue is fixed in versions 2.9.15 and 3.0.17.

In Progress® Kendo® UI for jQuery versions prior to 2026.4.1111, kendo.init() compiles data-* attribute values with new Function when an invalid JSON object is supplied. An attacker with low privileges who can control these attribute values can inject JavaScript that executes during declarative widget initialization when a user loads or interacts with an affected page. Successful exploitation can compromise the confidentiality and integrity of data accessible in the user's browser context. The issue was reported in version 2022.3.1109; the first affected release has not been established.

A stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in maintenance-appendcode-check.php in Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an authenticated manager to execute JavaScript in an administrator's browser. A manager can store a malicious tracker name and cause the tracker to appear in the append-code maintenance results. When an administrator opens the affected maintenance page, the tracker name is included in HTML without appropriate encoding. The issue is fixed in Revive Adserver 6.0.9 by HTML-encoding tracker names when displaying the maintenance results.

OpsTree REMS through 1.0.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers to inject scripts by uploading attachments with spoofed text/html Content-Type. Attackers can upload HTML files named like test.html.pdf that render in the REMS origin via Preview, executing JavaScript in victims' browsers.

Wallos 4.4.0 before 5.10.3 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in endpoints/cronjobs/sendnotifications.php that allows registered users to inject scripts via unescaped notification service responses. Attackers can point their Mattermost webhook URL or Web Push endpoint at a controlled server returning JavaScript, which executes in the administrator's session when sendnotifications.php is opened.

Missing authorization in PostgreSQL DROP OWNED allows a role to remove itself from restrictive row level security policies, thereby reading or modifying rows that the policy was intended to deny, via queries after the DROP OWNED.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

Inconsistent transition-capture state in PostgreSQL MERGE allows a table data modifier to make an AFTER trigger process the wrong new row, via a partitioned table MERGE that performs an INSERT before an UPDATE.  Within major versions 15-18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, and 15.20 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 15 are unaffected.

Improper protection in PostgreSQL INSERT ... ON CONFLICT on auto-updatable views allows an attacker having INSERT and UPDATE privileges on the view to read and modify every row in the view's base table, via iterated INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE.  This bypasses the view's WHERE condition, whether or not the view is a security_barrier view.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

@hono/node-server allows running the Hono application on Node.js. From 2.0.0 until 2.1.6, the WebSocket upgrade path resolves a raw request-target beginning with // against a base URL built from the Host header, causing the WHATWG URL parser to treat the request-target as a network-path reference and replace the host in c.req.url. Routing still uses the local WebSocket path, so an application that compares the Origin header with the origin of c.req.url, including checks implemented with csrf(), compares an attacker's origin with itself and accepts the connection. A page on another site can consequently open a WebSocket with the victim's cookies and read and send messages when the application uses upgradeWebSocket and trusts the host in c.req.url. Ordinary HTTP requests are not affected. This issue is fixed in version 2.1.6.

A flaw was found in Red Hat Quay. The v1 registry API error handler reflects the attacker-supplied image_id path segment in a response served as text/html, allowing a reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) attack. By tricking a user into visiting a specially crafted URL, a remote attacker can execute arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser within the Quay origin, potentially compromising the user's session.

Vvveb through 1.0.8.6 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows low-privilege author or vendor users to inject script by bypassing the regex blacklist in sanitizeHTML(). Attackers can save post or product content with unclosed event-handler tags or javascript: entities to execute script for anonymous visitors and admins, enabling session or CSRF-token theft.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users with Eye Exam edit permission to inject scripts via the Next Visit Orders PLAN[] field. Attackers can store a payload closing the textarea in view.php, executing JavaScript when another user opens the Eye Exam editor to steal session identifiers or clinical data.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows low-privileged patient portal users to inject JavaScript via the tableArgs field of the onsiteportalactivity API. Attackers can store a payload with spaces that breaks out of an unquoted data-delete-id attribute, executing script when providers click the delete button on the audit review page.

Zipline from 4.3.0 before 4.5.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated low-privilege users to inject HTML through unescaped embed settings in SSR meta tags. Attackers can set malicious embedTitle, embedDescription, embedSiteName, or embedColor values via PATCH /api/user to execute JavaScript in browsers of visitors opening their file view pages.

Zipline before 4.5.0 contains a stored open redirect vulnerability that allows authenticated users to set arbitrary short URL destinations by abusing missing scheme validation in POST /api/user/urls. Attackers can store javascript: URIs or attacker-controlled URLs as destinations, causing visitors of the trusted short link to be redirected to phishing or malware pages.

Axeloz Filesharing before 2.14.3 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users to inject script by storing raw HTML or javascript: Markdown links in bundle descriptions. Recipients viewing the public bundle preview page execute the script via Alpine x-html, letting attackers steal the owner_token from localStorage and issue owner-scoped requests against victim bundles.

Kalmia through 0.2.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows read-only authenticated users to upload HTML or SVG files via the upload-file endpoint without type restrictions. Attackers can share links to files served unauthenticated through the file get route, executing JavaScript in the admin origin to steal administrator JWTs from localStorage.

Keystatic through 0.6.9 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the DocumentRenderer component that allows authenticated content editors to inject scripts via unvalidated link href values. Editors can paste anchors with javascript: URLs into document fields, executing script when visitors click rendered links and stealing the keystatic-gh-access-token cookie.

Rowy through 3.0.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users with table write access to inject unsanitized HTML into Markdown cells. Attackers can store iframe, object, or form elements with javascript: URLs that execute when administrators view the table, stealing Firebase sessions.

Rowy through 3.0.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users with table write access to inject scripts via URL field links lacking scheme validation. Attackers can store values like javascript: URIs containing the string http in URL cells, executing script when victims click the open-link button to steal Firebase sessions.

qbee-agent is the device agent component of the qbee.io IoT device management platform. Prior to 2026.41, the unpackTar extraction logic in app/utils/tar.go validates cleaned archive entry paths with strings.HasPrefix(targetPath, destdirClean) without enforcing a path-separator boundary. When UseContext enables the Docker Compose build context path in app/configuration/bundle_docker_compose.go, a less-privileged archive supplier with delegated configuration and/or file-manager access can provide a sibling-prefix traversal entry that passes the check, causing utils.UnpackTar to create directories and regular files outside the intended context extraction directory with qbee-agent process privileges, despite the supplier lacking authority to write those sibling files. In deployments where only full device or fleet administrators can provide Docker Compose context archives, this behavior is hardening rather than a crossed security boundary. The demonstrated impact is limited to nearby cache or project paths sharing the destination prefix, may affect integrity or availability of qbee-agent-managed Docker Compose state, and does not establish arbitrary absolute-path writes or direct code execution. This issue is fixed in version 2026.41.

Silverstripe Framework is a PHP framework which powers the Silverstripe CMS. Prior to 6.2.13, the HTML sanitiser does not remove script-capable XHTML and XML data URIs from stored CMS content. A CMS author can save such content, and JavaScript executes in the browser of another user who views it. This issue is fixed in version 6.2.13.

Silverstripe Framework is a PHP framework which powers the Silverstripe CMS. Prior to 6.2.13, the HTML sanitiser does not remove SVG data URIs from stored CMS content even though SVG documents can execute script. A CMS author can save such content, and JavaScript executes in the browser of another user who views it. This issue is fixed in version 6.2.13.

phpMyFAQ before 4.1.12 and 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows registered users to inject javascript: links via FAQ comments. When the comment editor is enabled, Utils::parseUrl() strips https:// from sanitized hrefs, turning an allowed https://javascript:443/ link into executable script that runs on the shared admin origin when clicked.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 13.2 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user with owner-role permissions to execute arbitrary JavaScript in another user's browser through the Confluence integration due to improper input validation.

Filament Curator is a media picker plugin for Filament panels. From 3.0.0 until 3.7.9, 4.1.2, and 5.1.2, the Curator media panel accepts image/svg+xml files by default and stores and serves their markup inline without sanitization. An authenticated user with media-upload permission can store an SVG containing scripts, event-handler attributes, or javascript: URIs. When another panel user selects the View action, the SVG opens as a top-level browser document and its active content executes in the Filament application's origin. The script can perform authenticated same-origin actions as the viewing user and read same-origin data and script-accessible tokens. Panel thumbnails are not affected because they render through an image element that does not execute SVG script. This issue is fixed in versions 3.7.9, 4.1.2, and 5.1.2.

WWBN AVideo from 11.1 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows users with streaming permission to inject HTML by supplying an unvalidated url parameter to plugin/LiveLinks/play.php. Attackers can embed a --> sequence to escape the HTML comment in liveVideo.php, creating a shareable link that executes JavaScript in any visitor's session.

Craft CMS from 5.0.0 before 5.11.4 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows low-privilege control panel users to inject JavaScript by poisoning cached license data. Attackers can store a malicious licensed domain via the app/process-api-response-headers endpoint, which executes unescaped in administrators' dashboard license-mismatch warnings.

ScreenTinker before 3.2.4 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the GET /api/kiosk/:id/render endpoint that allows users with kiosk page edit rights to store javascript: URLs in page buttons. Attackers can trigger script execution in the dashboard origin when an administrator activates the button, hijacking the victim's session and taking full control of the instance.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. An authenticated remote user with a pending required security action, such as configuring multi-factor authentication (MFA), can bypass the mandatory action by submitting a specially crafted request to the consent endpoint without a valid session code. Keycloak incorrectly interprets the submission as a page refresh and completes the authentication process, allowing the user to access the application without fulfilling the required security policies.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with container edit permission could supply timestamps when creating containers and artifacts through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API. This could alter the timeline shown to analysts and cause configured data retention strategies to delete affected records earlier than intended.
The vulnerability is possible because the REST API accepts client-supplied values for timestamps that Splunk SOAR uses to order records and apply data retention.
The early deletion impact requires an applicable data retention strategy; the timeline impact does not.
For more information see Manage your PostgreSQL database with data retention strategies (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/6.4.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-system-health-and-performance/manage-your-postgresql-database-with-data-retention-strategies) in the Splunk documentation.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. This vulnerability allows an authenticated remote attacker to cause a denial of service by terminating active sessions of arbitrary users. When processing Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) documents that lack a root signature, Keycloak accepts the request as long as any assertion within the document is signed, without verifying its context or placement. An attacker holding a validly signed assertion can embed it into an unsigned logout request for another user, causing Keycloak to accept the forged request and terminate the victim's session.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. When an administrator revokes tokens by setting a not-before revocation cutoff, Keycloak fails to enforce this boundary when processing User-Managed Access (UMA) grant requests using ID token claims. An authenticated remote user with an active session can submit a previously revoked ID token to receive a fresh Requesting Party Token (RPT). This flaw allows an attacker to bypass token revocation and retain unauthorized access to protected resources.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. When processing token requests using the User-Managed Access (UMA) grant, Keycloak fails to verify whether a target client or resource server is enabled before issuing an authorization token. An authenticated remote user can exploit this flaw to obtain valid Requesting Party Tokens (RPTs) for disabled clients, bypassing administrative access controls and permissions restrictions.

Penpot 2.18.0 before 2.18.2 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users with edit rights to bypass the sanitize-svg-element blocklist using namespace-prefixed SVG elements. Attackers can upload SVGs containing elements like x:script or attributes like x:onload, which are served inline as image/svg+xml to run JavaScript in victims' Penpot sessions.

Admidio from 5.0.17 before 5.0.18 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users to inject JavaScript by saving a crafted value in their STREET profile field. Attackers can break out of the unencoded title attribute in members_assignment_data.php with an onmouseover handler that executes in the session of role managers hovering over the address icon.

Admidio from 5.0.16 before 5.0.18 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows users with folder upload rights to store JavaScript by uploading SVG files served inline. Attackers can upload a script-bearing SVG that downloadFile() serves as image/svg+xml inline without nosniff or CSP, executing on the Admidio origin for viewers including unauthenticated visitors.

Penpot 2.18.0 before 2.19.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the sanitize-svg function that allows authenticated users to bypass filtering through unescaped re-serialization. Attackers with file edit permission can upload SVGs using entity-encoded or CDATA-wrapped markup or attribute quote breakouts to execute JavaScript in the Penpot origin when victims open them.

A vulnerability has been found in Xuxueli xxl-job 3.5.0/3.5.1-SNAPSHOT. The affected element is an unknown function of the file JobLogController.java of the component Job Termination Endpoint. The manipulation leads to incorrect authorization. The attack can be initiated remotely. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A vulnerability was found in conductor-oss conductor up to 3.32.4/3.33.0/3.34.0-rc3/4.0.0-alpha.1. This issue affects the function WorkflowSystemTask.start of the file PlannerContextFetchTask.java of the component PLANNER_CONTEXT_FETCH Task Handler. The manipulation of the argument url results in server-side request forgery. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been made public and could be used. The researcher claims to have submitted a GHSA on the repository of the project.

A vulnerability was determined in floci-io Floci up to 2.4.0. Impacted is the function BuildspecParser.parseArtifacts of the file src/main/java/io/github/hectorvent/floci/services/codebuild/CodeBuildJsonHandler.java of the component Artifact Handler. This manipulation of the argument buildspecOverride.artifacts.base-directory causes path traversal. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

Due to Broken Access Control in SAP NetWeaver AS Java, an unauthenticated attacker could invoke affected SOAP operations exposed over HTTP without proper access control. Successful exploitation could allow disclosure of information accessible through the affected service, resulting in a low impact on confidentiality. Integrity and availability remain unaffected.

pgEdge Postgres MCP Server enables SQL queries against PostgreSQL databases through Model Context Protocol compatible clients. Prior to 1.1.0, the HTTP transport did not validate the Origin header on incoming requests. A user who visited an attacker-controlled page could be targeted through DNS rebinding, allowing the page to reach a locally running server and read schemas and query results from configured databases. The issue affected deployments with the HTTP transport enabled on a machine that also ran a browser, while the default stdio transport was not reachable through this path. This issue is fixed in version 1.1.0.

postal-mime before 4.2.1 contains an algorithmic complexity denial of service vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to cause excessive CPU consumption in the PostalMime.processLine() function by crafting deeply nested multipart email messages with boundary lines sharing long prefixes with open boundaries. Attackers can deliver a malicious email with nesting up to the default maxNestingDepth of 256, causing per-line parsing cost to scale as O(depth x shared prefix length) and blocking the Node.js event loop for seconds per message.

The sign-in of Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.2.22-pre2 through 6.3.7 takes for an account names that are not its address but under which the database's own comparison finds it, while the per-name lockout and the compromised-account hold are kept by the name as the client gave it. This allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to go on guessing an account's password beyond the lockout's threshold, and anyone who has the password of an account held for review to sign in to it. The per-name lockout (from 6.2.22-pre2; AccountLockoutThreshold in hMailServer.ini, 0, off, by default) locks a name after repeated failed sign-ins. The hold (from 6.3.4, where the compromised-account detection is set to enforce, which is not the default) refuses an account judged to have been taken over. Both are asked, before the password, of the name the client gave: trimmed, in lower case and with a domain alias or the default domain applied. The account whose password the sign-in then checks is whichever one the database finds under that name. The databases find an account under spellings that this key counts apart. MySQL and MariaDB find it under one with accented letters in place of plain ones, and MariaDB 11.8, in a database made before 6.3.4, also under one with full-width letters, with a single letter in place of a pair of plain ones, or with characters its comparison ignores in any number. SQL Server and SQL Server Compact find it under one with full-width letters or with characters their comparison ignores in any number, and SQL Server also under one with a single letter in place of a pair of plain ones, with a character of Latin-1 in place of a digit and, for an address holding letters of Latin-1 outside ASCII, under those letters in the other case, and, under an accent-insensitive collation, with accented letters. PostgreSQL finds it under one holding a letter whose lower case under the database's locale is a plain letter, and, for an address holding letters outside ASCII, under those letters in the other case; on the build for musl (from 6.3.6) the server's own lower case folds nearly all of these too. On every database, a domain alias saved with white space at the end of its name gives such a spelling too, and on every database but PostgreSQL so does an account's bare local part where the default domain was saved with spaces at its end and no other white space (neither is the default). Each such spelling has a lockout threshold of its own, so the lockout limits the guesses at an account only to its threshold times the number of the account's spellings. That is far beyond any threshold for most addresses on MySQL and MariaDB, and without limit on SQL Server, on SQL Server Compact, the database the Windows installer uses by default, and before 6.3.4 on MariaDB 11.8. A locked name is got round under another spelling. A held account is signed in to under another spelling with its password over IMAP, POP3 and SMTP AUTH, and, where they are turned on (off by default), over ManageSieve, the REST API and the webmail. IMAP LOGIN, offered as installed, carries such spellings on MySQL, MariaDB and SQL Server Compact, and, on SQL Server and PostgreSQL, for some addresses; the sign-ins that carry a name as UTF-8 carry them for the others on SQL Server, and on PostgreSQL for those holding one of the plain letters another letter lowers to or a letter outside ASCII with another case. The same lookup mapped to accounts the names given by an OAuth 2.0 token, a client certificate, a Kerberos ticket and an OpenID Connect or SAML identity provider, where those are set up (none is by default), so that a name an issuer gave to one party could sign in to another's account; OAuth 2.0 tokens were mapped so from 6.2.0, before the per-name lockout existed. A name holding a NUL character, carried from 6.3.0 on Linux and 6.3.3 on Windows, failed the statement on MySQL, MariaDB and PostgreSQL.

The auto-ban of Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.0.0-B1 through 6.3.7 can be kept from banning an address after repeated failed logons, which allows a remote unauthenticated attacker who can connect from two or more addresses to go on guessing account passwords - over SMTP AUTH, IMAP and POP3, and over ManageSieve, CalDAV/CardDAV and the REST API where those are turned on (off by default) - without being banned. When the failed logons counted from one address reach MaxInvalidLogonAttempts (3 by default), the server clears that address's count, saves an IP range that refuses the address for AutoBanMinutes (60 by default) and drops the connection. The range is named "Auto-ban: " followed by the user name of the logon that reached the limit, and no two ranges may have the same name. The server chooses the name by checking candidates as written - the name, then the name with a number, a random suffix or a GUID added - and only then cuts it to the 100 characters the database column holds, so that with a user name of 90 characters or more every candidate is the same once cut. While one range named after such a user name stands, every later ban named after a user name with the same first 90 characters therefore fails at the database: no range is saved, the address is not refused, and, its count having already been cleared, it is given the next full set of attempts. A user name of 78 to 89 characters makes later bans fail in the same way: from the second, the third or the twelfth on, depending on its length and the database, or, from 78 to 85 characters, by chance. An attacker who has once had an address banned under such a name can in this way keep guessing passwords from any other address, ending each set of attempts with a logon under a name of that kind; each failed save is reported in the server's error log (as the database error HM5032, and from 6.2.19 also as HM6099). On SQL Server a user name holding characters outside the database's code page has the same effect at any length, because the check compared names in that code page; that save is refused by the server's own check of the name, with no database error, and is reported only from 6.2.19 (HM6099). A user name holding a NUL character, which the web services listener's HTTP Basic sign-in (off by default) carries from 6.3.3 and, on the Linux builds, IMAP LOGIN, offered as installed, from 6.3.0, makes bans fail at any length: on MySQL, MariaDB and PostgreSQL the statements that check the name and save the range end at the character, so that every ban named after such a name fails, from the first and from a single address, and, its count having already been cleared, the address is given the next full set of attempts; on SQL Server and SQL Server Compact the name is bound only as far as the character, so that while one range under the part before it stands, every later ban named after such a name fails.
